osm_source.important_caveat: campaigns/ingolstadt_cooked_perception_v1/source/manifest.json documents that ingolstadt_authoritative.osm has building_way_count=1 (it is a roads-oriented Overpass export, essentially building-free). The pin's real building footprint data (5693 building ways / 19 relations) lives in a SEPARATE file, campaigns/ingolstadt_cooked_perception_v1/source/ingolstadt_buildings_overpass.json, which is Overpass JSON format -- NOT an .osm/.osm.xml/.pbf file OSM2World can consume directly. No existing converter from that Overpass-JSON buildings file to OSM XML was found in this codebase (osm_polygon_loader.py reads it directly for OpenDRIVE lane/building-footprint purposes, not via OSM2World). This run therefore reproduces the pipeline's actual, currently-wired OSM2World input exactly as main_pipeline.py would invoke it -- but that wiring does NOT currently route the pin's 5682-5693 real buildings through OSM2World. The resulting mesh is genuine full-map-extent clutter (retaining walls, surface areas, a small number of building/indoor objects incidentally tagged in the roads file) rather than a full building-volume reconstruction. Building a JSON->OSM-XML bridge to close this gap was judged out of scope for this task (task said 'run the EXISTING export path', not build a new converter) and is flagged here as a follow-up, not silently done or silently ignored.

scale_finding.title: Real map-scale data exposes an OSM2World renderer bug the tiny test window never hit
scale_finding.detail: Both the OBJ and GLB render passes hit 'ERROR: polygon must not not have duplicate points' (org.osm2world.util.exception.InvalidGeometryException) originating in org.osm2world.world.modules.building.indoor.IndoorModule$Elevator, triggered by degenerate (duplicate-point) polygons on OSM ways w462314990, w359550749, w359550745 (indoor/elevator-tagged features somewhere in the roads file's incidental building/indoor tagging). In the OBJ pass this was non-fatal (OSM2World's FaultTolerantIterationUtil skips the offending object and continues -- 3 objects silently dropped, rest of the scene rendered fine). In the GLB pass, the same error caused Blender's own gltf importer to reject the resulting GLB outright with a UTF-8 JSON parse error, so the runner's built-in GLB validation correctly caught and excluded it. Net effect: OBJ/FBX path is unaffected and usable; GLB output is not currently usable from this source file at full scale. This is a genuine, previously-unobserved finding -- the 2026-08-04 test window (773KB, 4670 nodes) apparently did not include these 3 problem ways.

stage_2_blender_fbx.note_on_object_count_delta: OSM2World's raw OBJ had 72 'o'/'g' groupings; Blender's wm.obj_import materialized 61 MESH objects (some groupings were empty/zero-face and were not imported as separate mesh objects -- consistent with the 3 objects OSM2World's fault-tolerant iteration dropped during the polygon-duplicate-point errors, plus a small number of non-mesh group markers).

stage_3_fbx_roundtrip.method: Re-imports the FBX in a second, clean, headless Blender process (separate from the conversion session) and diffs object/vertex/face/UV/material/bounds inventory against the conversion manifest.

overall_verdict: PASS: full-coverage OSM2World->Blender->FBX export succeeded end-to-end against the current pin's actual OSM source, and fbx_roundtrip.py's independent re-import verification confirms zero geometry loss/drift through the FBX export/import round-trip. Two concrete findings: (1) a real OSM2World renderer bug (degenerate elevator polygon) that only surfaces at full map scale and currently blocks the GLB output (OBJ/FBX path unaffected); (2) the pipeline's existing OSM2World wiring is fed the roads-oriented OSM file (building_way_count=1), not the pin's actual 5693-building Overpass JSON, so this export is genuinely full-map-extent but is NOT a full building-volume reconstruction of the pin's buildings -- closing that gap needs a new Overpass-JSON-to-OSM-XML bridge that does not currently exist.
